contrast sensitivity is a better predictor of cognitive performance in high sensory-demand than in low sensory-demand tasks and that contrast sensitivity accounts for more of the variability in high sensory demand than in low sensory demand tasks.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between sensory and cognitive function in aging and the role sensory function plays in cognitive performance.
the relationship between cognitive and sensory function, and its implications for understanding the mechanisms of cognitive decline in normal aging.
the role of sensory function in cognitive and everyday functioning in aging.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sensory and cognitive functions in aging are interrelated.
the sensory system, in this case the visual system, is a critical component for the cognitive system and that the cognitive system is dependent on the sensory system.
contrast sensitivity plays an important role in cognitive aging, but it is unclear if it is a cause, a correlate, a consequence, a marker, or a confound.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sensory system may be a useful index for assessing the integrity of the brain and the potential for cognitive decline.
contrast sensitivity may be an index of neurological health and may also directly influence cognitive performance in older adults.
contrast sensitivity, as a marker of visual function, is a better predictor of verbal than spatial performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sensory function may be a better index of cognitive health than is commonly appreciated.
visual function may be a useful index of cognitive health.
